facts.text: The overture’s soft final chords were a setup: they lead straight into G minor, the key of Ilia’s scene.
evidence: These chords, soft and tentative, turn out not to be a resolution of the overture in the tonic but chords in the dominant of G minor, which is the home key of the scene that immediately follows.

facts.text: Recitative comes two ways here: “secco”, with just harpsichord and cello, and orchestral “accompagnato”, which Mozart handles masterfully.
evidence: the secco and stromentato recitatives
Basso continuo (harpsichord and violoncello)
he demonstrated a mastery of orchestral color, accompanied recitatives, and melodic line
recitativo secco ("dry", accompanied only by continuo, typically cello and harpsichord)
recitativo accompagnato (which uses an orchestra to accompany the singer)

is the 2017 Richard Tucker Music Foundation Award Winner

facts.text: Mozart wrote Idamante for a castrato. Alice Coote, known for trouser roles, also sang him in San Francisco in 2008.

facts.text: Elettra, jealous of Ilia: “I can feel you all in my heart, furies of the dark hell.”

facts.text: Shipwreck! Mozart builds this scene almost exactly like the storm scene in Gluck’s Iphigénie en Tauride.
evidence: the shipwreck scene towards the end of act 1 is almost identical to the structure and dramatic working-out of a similar scene in Gluck's Iphigénie en Tauride

facts.text: Mozart was 24 when he wrote Idomeneo, his third opera seria, for the Munich court carnival.
evidence: Mozart's third and finest "opera seria," composed when he was 24
commissioned in 1780 by Karl Theodor, Elector of Bavaria for a court carnival

facts.text: Ponnelle’s frame: classical Roman columns, a broad flight of steps, and shifting backdrops of Piranesi-style ruins.
evidence: Ponnelle's use of classical Roman columns framing the stage, a broad flight of steps between, and a constantly shifting series of backdrops of monumental buildings and similar structures in ruins, all clearly derived from Piranesi

facts.text: Arbace today: British baritone Alan Opie, who shared Grammys for recordings of Peter Grimes and Die Meistersinger.
evidence: In March 2017, he performed the role of Arbace

facts.text: Four solo winds join Ilia: flute, oboe, horn, bassoon. Her first singer, Dorothea Wendling, was a flautist’s wife.
facts.attribution: Mozart to his father Leopold, Munich, 8 Nov 1780, planning this aria “in concert with four wind instruments”
evidence: Munich, Nov. 8, 1780.
"Se il padre perdei, in te lo ritrovo"
an aria andantino here in concert with four wind instruments, viz. flute, hautboy, horn, and bassoon
“Ilia” was sung by Dorothea (I) Wendling, née Spurni, wife of the traverse flautist Johann Baptist

facts.text: Mozart on this quartet: “there is no single thing in my opera with which I am so pleased.”
facts.attribution: Mozart to his father Leopold, Munich, 27 Dec 1780
evidence: Munich, Dec 27, 1780.
there is no single thing in my opera with which I am so pleased as with this quartet

facts.text: Mozart added this march so the king can enter with his whole suite. Scored simply, to be played mezza voce.
facts.attribution: Mozart to his father Leopold, Munich, 3 Jan 1781
evidence: he must come accompanied by his whole suite. A march must necessarily be introduced here, so I have composed a very simple one for two violins, tenor, bass, and two hautboys, to be played a mezza voce, and during this time the King appears

facts.text: Mozart’s plan for Neptune: three trombones (heard only here) and two horns, placed with the voice. The orchestra falls silent.
facts.attribution: Mozart to his father Leopold, Munich, 3 Jan 1781
evidence: The accompaniment of the underground music consists merely of five instruments, namely, three trombones and two French horns, which are placed on the spot whence the voice proceeds. The whole orchestra is silent at this part.
3 trombones (only accompanying the off-stage voice of Neptune in act 3)

facts.text: Home to D major, the overture’s key. Mozart first closed an opera this way here, then in every one after.
evidence: The overture, in D major and common time
